questions.q: The number of integral values of a for which the inequality $3 - \left|x - a\right| > x^{2}$ is satisfied by atleast one negative x, must be equal to
questions.solution:
Given inequality is
$3 - \left|x - a\right| > x^{2} . . . \left($1\right)$

$⇒ \left|x - a\right| < 3 - x^{2}$

or~$- 3 + x^{2} < x - a < \left(3 - x^{2}\right)$

or $x^{2} - x + a - 3 < 0 \left(2\right)$

and~$x^{2} + x - \left(a + 3\right) < 0 . . . \left(3\right)$

If~ $\alpha,\beta \left(\alpha< \beta\right)$ be the real and unequal roots of the corresponding equation of Eq. \left(1\right)$~for all $x \in \left(\alpha,\beta\right).Since Eq. \left($1\right)$~will have at least one negative solution. The corresponding equation of \left(2\right)$~and \left(3\right)$~are

$x^{2} - x + a - 3 = 0 . . . \left($4\right)$

and~$x^{2} + x - \left(a + 3\right) = 0 . . . \left($5\right)$
respectively.

Both Eqs. \left(4\right)$~and \left($5\right)$~should have real and unequal roots, then

$1 - 4 $\cdot$1 $\cdot \left(a - 3\right) > 0 & 1 + 4 \cdot \left(a + 3\right) > 0$

i.e.,~$a - \dfrac{13}{4} . . . \left(6\right)$

Roots of Eq. \left(6\right)$~are~$\dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{\left(13 - 4a\right)}}{2}$

One of these will be negative provided the condition below

$13 - 4a > 1$

i.e.,~$a < 3 . . . \left($7\right)$

So, it has one negative root.

Combining Eqs. \left(6\right)$~and \left($7\right)$, we get

$- $\dfrac{13}{4}$< a < 3$

$∴  $~Integral values of a are~ $- 3, - 2, - 1, 0, 1, 2 .$

Total number~$= 6 .$

questions.q: If \left(x^{2} + 5x + 5\right)x + 5 = 1$ \text{ and } then the number of integers satisfying this equation is$
questions.solution:
Given that,& \left(x^{2} + 5x + 5\right)x + 5 = 1$

This is possible when~$x^{2} + 5x + 5 \ne 0 \text{ and } x + 5 = 0$~or~$x^{2} + 5x + 5 = 1$~or~$x^{2} + 5x + 5 = - 1 \text{ and } x + 5 = eveninteger$

Case1,~$x + 5 = 0$

$⇒ x = - 5$

And for this value of~$x$,~$x^{2} + 5x + 5 \ne 0$

Case2,~$x^{2} + 5x + 5 = 1$

$⇒ x^{2} + 5x + 4 = 0$

$⇒ \left(x + 1\right)\left(x + 4\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = - 1, - 4$

Case3,~$x^{2} + 5x + 5 = - 1$

$⇒ x^{2} + 5x + 6 = 0$

$⇒ \left(x + 2\right)\left(x + 3\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = - 2, - 3$

But for~$x = - 2,$~we get~$x + 5 = 3$~which is not even.

Hence, the number of integers satisfying this equation is~$4$.

$

Clearly by modulus function~property~\left|x + 2\right| \ge 0 \text{ and } \left|x + 3\right| \ge 0$~and~$x \ne - 2, - 3$.

Now, $x^{2} + 6x - 7 < 0$.

$⇒ x^{2} + 7x - x - 7 < 0$

$⇒ \left(x + 7\right)\left(x - 1\right) < 0$

Using Sign Scheme for this expression,

$⇒ x \in \left(- 7, 1\right) - \left\{- 3, - 2\right\}$

So, integers are \left\{- 6, - 5, - 4, - 1, 0\right\}$.

So, total number of integral~values of~$x = 5$.

questions.q: If $m, n$ are any two integers and~$m \text{ and } n$~are related as $m = n^{2} - n$,~Then the expression~$m^{2} - 2m$ is always divisible by
questions.solution:
Given,& $m = n^{2} - n$

$m = n \left(n - 1\right) .$

$m^{2} - 2m = m\left(m - 2\right)$

$= n \left(n - 1\right) \left(n^{2} - n - 2\right)$

$= n \left($n - 1\right)\left($n + 1\right) \left(n - 2\right)$

$m^{2} - 2m = \left(n - 2\right) \left(n - 1\right)n \left($n + 1\right)$.

It is the product of $4$~consecutive integers.

$∴ m^{2} - 2m$ must be divisible by $24$.

$

questions.q: If $\dfrac{6x^{2} - 5x - 3}{x^{2} - 2x + 6} \le 4,$ then the least and highest values of $4x^{2}$ are
questions.solution:
We have,

$\dfrac{6x^{2} - 5x - 3}{x^{2} - 2x + 6} \le 4$

$⇒ \dfrac{6x^{2} - 5x - 3 - 4x^{2} + 8x - 24}{x^{2} - 2x + 6} \le 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{2x^{2} + 3x - 27}{x^{2} - 2x + 6} \le 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(2x + 9\right)\left(x - 3\right)}{\left(x - 1\right)2 + 5} \le 0$

Now,~\left(x - 1\right)2 + 5 > 0, ∀ x \in R$.

So,

$2x^{2} + 3x - 27 \le 0$

$⇒ \left(2x + 9\right)\left(x - 3\right) \le 0$

~$⇒ - \dfrac{9}{2} \le x \le 3$

Now, at~$x = - \dfrac{9}{2}$,~$4x^{2} = 4 \times \left(\dfrac{- 9}{2}\right)2 = 81$

And, at~$x = 3$,~$4x^{2} = 36$

Therefore, greatest value of~$4x^{2}$~is~$81$.

And, least value of~$4x^{2}$~is $0$~occurs at~$x = 0$.

$

\Rightarrow & x(\log 2+\log 3)=x \log 7+4 \log 7 \\

questions.q: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the least positive integers such that for all $n \in N, n^3+\alpha n$ is divisible by 3 and $n^3-\beta n$ is divisible by 6 , then $\alpha+\beta=$
questions.solution: If for all $n \in N, n^3+\alpha n$ is divisible by 3 , then for $n=1$ also it is divisible by 3 , so the least positive integral value of $\alpha=2$ And, since for all $n \in N, n^3-\beta n$ is divisible by 6 , then for $n=1$ also it is divisible by 6 , so the least positive integral value of $\beta=1$. So, $\alpha+\beta=2+1=3$. Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.q: Solve $\log_{10}  \left({2}^{x} +1\right) + x = \log_{10} \left(6\right) + x\log_{10}\left(5\right).$
questions.solution:
The given expression is&
$\log_{10} \left({2}^{x} +1\right) + x = \log_{10} \left(6\right) + x\log_{10}\left(5\right)$

We know that~$\log_{\mathrm{m}}\left(x\right) + \log_{\mathrm{m}}\left(y\right) = \log_{\mathrm{m}} \left(xy\right) & \log_{\mathrm{m}} \left($x\right) + $\log_{\mathrm{m}}\left($y\right) = $\log_{\mathrm{m}}\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right)

$⇒ $\log_{10}\left({2}^{x} +$1\right) = x \left(\log_{10} \left(5\right) - \log_{10}\left(10\right)\right) + \log_{10}\left(6\right)$

$⇒ \log_{10} \left({2}^{x} +1\right) = - \log_{10} \left(2\right)x + \log_{10}\left(6\right)$

$⇒ \log_{10} \left({2}^{x} +1\right) + \log_{10} \left({2}^{x}\right) = \log_{10}\left(6\right)$

$⇒ \log_{10} \left[ \left({2}^{x}\right) \left({2}^{x} +1\right)\right] = \log_{10}\left(6\right)$

Taking antilog on both sides, we get

$⇒ \left({2}^{x}\right) \left({2}^{x} +1\right) = 6$

$⇒ \left({2}^{x}\right)2 + {2}^{x} - 6 = 0$

$⇒ \left({2}^{x} -2\right)\left({2}^{x} +3\right) = 0$

$⇒ {2}^{x} = 2 ⇒ x = 1$~ ~ ~ \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } Hence, \text{ and } $x = 1$

questions.q: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the greatest divisors of $n \left(n^{2} - 1\right)$ and $2n \left(n^{2} + 2\right)$ respectively for all~$n \in N$, then $\alpha\beta =$
questions.solution:
For $n \in N ⇒ n = 1, 2, 3 \ldots$

The values of $n \left(n^{2} - 1\right)$ are

$n = 1 ⇒ 1\left(1 - 1\right) = 0$

$n = 2 ⇒ 2\left(4 - 1\right) = 2\left(3\right) = 6$

$n = 3 ⇒ 3 \left(9 - 1\right) = 24 \ldots$

The values of $2n\left(n^{2} + 2\right)$ are,

$n = 1 ⇒ 2\left(1 + 2\right) = 6$

$n = 2 ⇒ 2\left(2\right)\left({2}^{2} +2\right) = 4\left(6\right) = 24$

$n = 3 ⇒ 2\left(3\$right)\left({3}^{2} +$2\right) = $6\left($11\right) = 66 \ldots$

$∴$~Greatest divisors of~\alpha and \beta~are both~$6$,

$∴ $\alpha\beta = \left($6\$right)\left($6\right) = 36$
